title: JSON Schema
subtitle: Every work-order contract, tool definition and generated function surface in my estate is a JSON Schema, and schemas compile into dispatch at build time.

stats.label: semantic rules checking each API reference
lines of Rust in the harness validator

lede: Long agent runs drift when the handoffs between agents are prose, because each agent reinterprets what the last one meant. In AgentOS I made every handoff a contract and chose JSON Schema as the contract language. The .schema.json contracts cover work-order sources, authoring plans, work packages and the structured output of model checkers. Every seam is checked on both sides, so a malformed artefact cannot pass through a component that trusts its upstream. The PostgreSQL work graph and its schemas are the truth; Markdown views are generated from them, and edits to those views are discarded. Work-order authoring starts from an operator-only source document.
quote: I put the checks where a bad artefact would otherwise pass unnoticed.
evidence: Contract-driven agent handoffs: 33 JSON Schema contracts in AgentOS, each seam checked by both producer and consumer.
Structured output for LLMs: flat, closed verdict schemas so model checkers return data instead of drifting prose.
Evidence-gated API integration: a field enters an API manifest only once a successful call to the real API returned it, checked by 12 semantic rules.
Input validation at scale: about 2,000 lines of Rust validating every tool call as the first step of the harness.
author: Corey James
